title: Hospital Days Reversed Before the Charge and the Medicare Part A Rate-Year Correction
content:
**Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage — hospital days and the rate-year correction.** A day reversed as a hospital day is not a covered day: when the corrected block's booked-days entry carries a hospital-day reversal posted on or before the date the charge was posted, its reversed days inside the corrected block come off the days the rate-year correction counts before the supplemental effective date, all of them when its last reversed day falls before that date, those from its first reversed day up to the day before the date when the date falls after its first reversed day and on or before its last, and none otherwise; without such a reversal, none come off.

### Basis Q&A

**What record is read?** A reversal of booked days with the reason hospital day, posted against the corrected block's own booked-days entry; its span runs from its first to its last reversed day. A reversal posted after the date of the resident's charge does not count for this rule.

**How many days come off when the supplemental effective date falls inside the span?** The days from the first reversed day up to the day before the date.

**And when the date falls after the span, or before it?** After the last reversed day, every reversed day inside the corrected block; on or before the first, none.

*Hypothetical worked example:* a hospital-day reversal covers the 17th to the 19th. With a supplemental effective date of the 18th, one day (the 17th) comes off; with the 20th, three days; with the 16th, none.
